scope: Read-only diagnosis of recurring owned Chromium startup failures. No native job, local browser, build, release, timeout change, resource-policy change, or acceptance promotion.

current_run.first_boundary_failure: owned_cdp_endpoint_timeout at cdp_connect, before any SEO target or panel action
current_run.acceptance_credit: none; six selected cases, zero executed targets

prior_sibling.result: spawn observed, 154 endpoint polls over 5022 ms, endpoint absent, CPU_PENDING after startup timeout, child exit 1, final resource-invalid, all 16 cases zero steps
prior_sibling.D168_boundary: The successful-child pending recovery branch was not exercised because the child failed. The separately documented valid local Settings retest closed D168 only at its infrastructure gate, without proving real-host CPU recovery.

source_contract.owned_cdp: connectOwnedCdp has a timeoutMs argument but defaults to fixed DEADLINE_MS=5000; runNativeSidepanelQa does not pass a timeoutMs value. ENOENT reads are polled every 25 ms. The timeout occurs before endpoint record, process-owner, or socket checks.
source_contract.existing_diagnostic: runNativeSidepanelQa can observe DevToolsActivePort for startupEndpointObservationMs after the 5-second timeout, but only when given a callback and positive observation window. The startup-resource-diagnostic route supplies a 15-second window from the existing resource policy and runs headed Chromium. The failed guest-seo route did not supply this callback, and its seo_resource_diagnostic flag adds guard process bracketing without enabling post-timeout endpoint observation.
source_contract.prior_diagnostic_result: Intel run 37710954422 connected CDP after 4894 ms from spawn and never entered post-timeout observation; it used headed Chromium and an older 0.2.391 artifact. Its elapsed span includes more than endpoint polling and establishes no safe margin or cause for current headless failures.

causal_limits: 116 polls and longest read 75 ms rule out an entirely stalled polling loop during the five-second wait, but do not show why Chromium did not publish the endpoint.
Null child exit and signal fields are snapshots, not proof the child stayed alive for the entire wait.
The process attribution snapshot after CPU_PENDING lists many macOS host daemons and Chromium at low sampled CPU; it cannot assign a causal CPU share over the preceding five-second endpoint wait.
CPU_PENDING occurred before the logged timeout and the final guard decision was invalid. This neither proves host load caused endpoint delay nor permits acceptance credit.

falsifiable_hypotheses.cause: Cold Chromium startup publishes the endpoint just after five seconds
falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: The owned endpoint appears during the existing bounded post-timeout observation before child exit, with a healthy or independently classified resource journal.

falsifiable_hypotheses.cause: Chromium stalls or exits before publishing the endpoint
falsifiable_hypotheses.prediction: No endpoint appears throughout the same observation, or an observed child exit precedes endpoint creation.
Comparable fresh runs show endpoint publication tracking measured host pressure and process attribution; a single pressure snapshot cannot establish this.

smallest_runnable_discriminator.precondition: Wait for the existing B native job to finish and root to authorize the reserved A slot; do not dispatch an unchanged acceptance retry.
smallest_runnable_discriminator.source_step: Wire the existing 15-second post-timeout endpoint observation into the guest-seo diagnostic-only path when seo_resource_diagnostic=true, preserving headed=false, the exact 0.2.407 artifact, the 5000 ms CDP deadline, ownership checks, and every resource threshold. Record only safe endpoint/exit observations in a diagnostic receipt; never turn a late endpoint or an invalid journal into acceptance credit.
smallest_runnable_discriminator.test_step: Run one guarded macos-15-intel guest-seo diagnostic with development run 37754055905/artifact 11539827040, seo_resource_diagnostic=true, full scope and Airbnb fixture, retaining the startup observation, BROWSER_STARTUP_FAILURE if any, and current-run package/browser/guest resource journals.
smallest_runnable_discriminator.interpretation: A late endpoint supports the cold-launch timing hypothesis; persistent absence or child exit points to a Chromium/host stall. A successful connection without timeout is a bounded non-reproduction only. None alone proves the underlying cause or product behavior.
